```{r}

dept_abbrv = c("Accountancy", "Economics", "Entrepreneurship", "Finance", "Information Systems & Analytics", "Marketing", "Management")
scrape_proffessors = function(abbrv){
  
  dept_url = paste0('https://miamioh.edu/fsb/directory/?up=/query/all/all/', URLencode(abbrv), '/all')


webpage = rvest::read_html(dept_url)

#DEPARTMENT

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1)") |> rvest::html_text2()->department


#NAME

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_text2()->name


webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3)") |> rvest::html_text2()->roles

#WEBSITE
webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_attr("href")->website

df = data.frame(department = department, name = name, position = roles, website = website)


return(df)
}

test = scrape_proffessors(abbrv = "Finance")

# to use functions from purr, we will use a map_*() or a map2_*(), or a pmap_*()
# map uses a function that takes a single input (or you are only chaning a single input)
# map2 uses a function that takes two inputs
# pmap>=3
# after the _, you put the type of object you are getting back

courses_df_from = purrr::map_df(.x = dept_abbrv, .f = scrape_proffessors)

head(courses_df_from)

```
